newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 8.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

-Sung Hae-rim, estranged wife of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, is staying in a Beijing villa under the protection of China and North Korea after moving there from Moscow. She has been the subject of much interest and mystery after South Korean press reported her defection to the West earlier this year.
- South Korea to host 2002 world cup opening ceremony, Japan to stage final match, according to FIFA. (This was also the leading story in both the Korea Times and Korea Herald newspapers.)
- Prices of petroleum products, gas utility to be raised toward end of year.

- Government and ruling party move to initiate a bill to provide heavy punishment against those who sell alcoholic beverage and cigarettes to juveniles. The punishment calls for a two-year prison term or fine of 10 million won.

- Gong Ro-myung's surprise resignation as foreign minister is linked to his personal history of being forced to join the North Korean people's army during the Korean war, Prime Minister Lee Soo-song disclosed during a parliamentary session.
